值得閱讀的理由

  • 快速梳理《攻殼機動隊》三十多年來各經典改編版本（押井守劇場版、神山健治SAC版、Arise前傳）的演變軌跡與核心特色。
  • 深入解析本作如何奠定現代賽博龐克美學，並以探討義體化、記憶與「靈魂（Ghost）」哲學啟發《駭客任務》等全球影視經典。
  • 了解公安九課成員性格刻畫的轉變，以及人氣吉祥物「塔奇克馬」與各大動畫團隊背後的精彩歷史。

摘要

賽博龐克殿堂之作的起源與三大基石

講者井川指出，由漫畫家士郎正宗於1989年打造的《攻殼機動隊》擁有極為多元且風格各異的改編體系。不論作品如何演變，其核心始終圍繞三大基石：未來世界、主角草薙素子以及專門打擊高科技犯罪的公安九課。這部作品不僅是日本動漫史上的傳奇IP，更是現代賽博龐克世界觀的重要奠基者。

1995年押井守電影版：奠定哲學思考與視覺巔峰

1995年由押井守執導、Production I.G製作的首部動畫電影，確立了大眾對該系列冷冽且充滿哲學性的深刻印象。該片深刻探討了當肉體完全被機械義體取代、記憶皆能偽造時，究竟何為「人」的本質，傳達出軀殼內的「Ghost」（靈魂與意識）才是生命存在的終極證明。片中精緻的手繪機械動態，以及素子開啟熱光學迷彩躍下高樓的經典分鏡，日後深深啟發了《駭客任務》等好萊塢鉅作。

神山健治執導的《SAC》：走向群戲魅力與人性化刻畫

在續作《無罪》製作延宕期間，導演神山健治打造了電視動畫《Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex》（SAC）。該作巧妙平衡了哲學沉重感與美式影集般的快節奏動作風格，不僅讓草薙素子展現出自信性感的女王氣場，更給予德古沙、荒卷課長等公安九課成員充分發揮的空間，並確立了人氣吉祥物塔奇克馬（思考戰車）的地位，成為奠定Production I.G業界聲譽的里程碑作品。

跨界聯動與前傳《Arise》的全新風貌

除經典動畫系列外，該IP也透過遊戲跨界聯動將賽博龐克風格與戰車載具融入互動娛樂中。2013年由黃瀨和哉執導的劇場版前傳《Ghost in the Shell: Arise》，則呈現了草薙素子加入公安九課前的軍旅時期。這部作品塑造出更具少女感、行事衝動且富有青春氣息的全新素子形象，展現了傳奇科幻IP不斷推陳出新的生命力。

================================================

Hi everyone, I'm Jingchuan. I'm sure you've all heard of the name "Ghost in the Shell," right? But I bet not many of you have actually seen it. However, you probably know that this series seems to have a ton of versions, and every one of them is quite different. In Japanese manga, copyrights largely belong to the original author, so it's usually hard for an IP to have so many different art styles and interpretations. Like Conan or Crayon Shin-chan, they've kept more or less the same image for decades, but Ghost in the Shell is uniquely magical in how it evolves. So today, let's quickly get. to know how many versions of Ghost in the Shell there actually are, plus I have some cool collaborations to share with you, so stay tuned. OK, if you like this kind of summary-style content , I've previously made videos on the history of Persona protagonists and Yakuza; feel free to check them out. Likes, subscriptions, and Super Thanks are all appreciated. Alright, 3, 2, 1. Let's dive in. Ghost in the Shell was originally a manga created by Masamune Shirow in 1989. If you're a casual viewer who has no idea what it's about,. just remember these three keywords: 1. A futuristic world, 2. Motoko Kusanagi, 3. Public Security Section 9. In a nutshell, Ghost in the Shell is the story of the protagonist Motoko Kusanagi, known as "The Major," who belongs to Public Security Section 9 and fights crime in a future world. No matter how this IP evolves, this baseline remains constant. In 1995, 31 years ago, Ghost in the Shell got its first animation adaptation, turned into a film by Production I.G. The title was. very simple: "Ghost in the Shell," and it was, of course, directed by Mamoru Oshii. To this day, this version remains the main impression the general public has of the series—cold, serious, and philosophical. It is largely one of the pioneers of today's popular cyberpunk worldview. Wait, if it's not Ghost in the Shell, then it's Blade Runner, right? Blade Runner provided that messy, rain-soaked, Asian-inspired aesthetic filled with neon signs, while Ghost in the Shell did more to popularize the concept of human body modification. Yes, so. without Ghost in the Shell, there would be no Cyberpunk 2077, okay? A big focus of this film is that the Major's body is almost entirely replaced by machine parts. She feels very cold and distant, prioritizing her missions above all else, just like a robot. Those who know a bit about the original work should know this is a huge departure from it, right? We will discuss this later, but this change serves to emphasize the core theme the film explores: once your.

entire body is no longer made of flesh, what exactly is it that keeps you human ? In a world where even memories can be fabricated, how can you be sure you are the person who has truly lived your life, rather than a replica whose data was uploaded just yesterday? If you grasp the message the film intends to convey, you will understand why this work is titled "Ghost in the Shell." Your body is ultimately just a shell; what truly matters is the consciousness , the "Ghost," inside. As long as it remains, it is the greatest proof that you are alive. In short, the 1995 Mamoru Oshii version is undoubtedly a cinematic masterpiece. Hollywood blockbusters like The Matrix were clearly deeply influenced by this film, and many scenes later became iconic moments that successors vied to pay homage to. Especially that most classic scene of the Major activating her thermoptic camouflage and slowly descending—future adaptations always. find a way to recreate it when given the chance! The incredibly detailed mechanical gunfight animation and the painstakingly hand-drawn mechanical movements remain, even today, a form of unparalleled, exquisite art. Following the massive success of the '95 Oshii version, I.G immediately threw themselves into the production of the sequel, Innocence. But as fans know, the production of Innocence was severely delayed, the budget ballooned, and worst of all, it flopped at the box office after its release. Back then,. the entire Production I.G company nearly went bankrupt, so while waiting for Innocence, I.G decided to develop another animated version of Ghost in the Shell. Little did they know they would create a classic to rival the films: Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex, directed by Kenji Kamiyama. The overall feel of SAC is as if it sits right between Oshii’s version and Masamune Shirow’s original manga. It isn't as somber as the films, nor as lighthearted as the manga; watching it feels like a sci-fi action series with. a very American TV show vibe. The title reflects the show's format— "Stand Alone Complex"—but what does that mean? "Stand Alone" refers to simple, standalone cases that conclude in a single episode, while "Complex" refers to the larger, main story arcs that require multiple episodes to unfold. Now, speaking of the Major in SAC, although she is still voiced by Atsuko Tanaka, her performance feels much more "human," no longer just a half-human, half-machine cyborg exploring the.

boundaries of humanity. This version of the Major is a confident, cool, and sexy queen. Motoko Kusanagi's outfits are eye-catching, and there are even some scenes that are super explicit with fan service. Anyway, enough about that. When it comes to Stand Alone Complex, I think its most important contribution is giving every member of Public Security Section 9 a chance to be known and loved by the audience. If you only watch the movie version,. it’s easy to get the impression that only Motoko and Batou really matter. But in SAC, you get the Major’s boss Aramaki, the least augmented and most " human" Togusa, plus Ishikawa, Saito, Borma, Pazu, and the others. And among them, the most important are certainly the Tachikomas. That’s right, these little tanks that look like hermit crabs were cut from the movie to maintain its tone, but they are absolutely the series 'mascots, even if their names were changed to Tachikoma. for various corporate reasons and their color turned blue. In short, I would say Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex was a career-defining work for Production I.G, because where did I.G's different production lines and I.G. Sixth Division come from? That's right, Ghost in the Shell. The most famous among them is none other than I.G. Sixth Division, which handled the best works and later became the powerhouse WIT Studio. Futuristic sci-fi police thrillers like this one became the main. impression of I.G for a very long time. For instance, Psycho-Pass was clearly inspired by SAC, at least until they realized how profitable "pretty boys" are. Now, we can also meet the Major in the world of Tower of Fantasy! This Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex collaboration officially begins on October 28th. Tower of Fantasy itself has a bit of a cyberpunk world-building style, so this collaboration with Ghost in the Shell is a perfect match. It adds a brand new collab pet Tachikoma,. "Motoko," as well as a collab vehicle, the Tachikoma, and five different paint jobs. My favorite is this heavier armored version. SYNCED is an incredibly satisfying multiplayer co-op action game. This collaboration even features an exclusive four-player mode for Ghost in the Shell—it's brilliant ! You and your friends can pilot Tachikomas, shooting, gathering resources, and upgrading while you compete. It’s absolutely a blast. The Halloween event "Phantom Night" is making a strong return. Collect puzzles , challenge bosses, and explore mysterious pumpkins—there's so much fun festive content waiting for you to discover. The level cap has been raised to 80! Once you break through this.

threshold, the game prepares a brand-new adventure chapter, " Redemption Sanctum," and a new map, " The Sanctum," where the long-awaited antagonist Conrad finally makes an appearance. In short, this Ghost in the Shell collaboration update is definitely not just about adding a few pets or vehicles; it’s a comprehensive major upgrade with new storylines, new dungeons, and new explorable areas. There's also the new Pilgrim gear, so it doesn't matter if you haven't played SYNCED for a while. The returning player event helps adventurers catch up to the top tier in an instant. Returning players can use the level-boost perk to reach a maxed-out state at level 70, so you can. join everyone else and push to level 80 immediately. Plus, by staying active for seven consecutive days, you can claim high-tier gear and various custom resource bundles, making catching up completely stress-free. Whether you’re a total newbie or a seasoned veteran, now is the perfect time to jump in or return. Entering the 2010s, Production I.G successfully developed several new hits, and it felt like Ghost in the Shell's mission had reached a temporary conclusion. That was until 2013's Ghost in the Shell: Arise, directed by Kazuchika Kise. This. version...well, as you can all tell, its biggest label is that the art style is essentially "Naruto." Yes, the character designs were by Takayuki Takadera. This naturally caused some dissatisfaction among old-school fans, but looking at Naruto in 2026, he doesn't even look like the original anymore—more like Kaiju No. 8—so it doesn't seem that bad now, right? This is a theatrical series spanning five works, with a different positioning than before. It leans toward a prequel, telling the story of Motoko Kusanagi. during her military days before joining Public Security Section 9. So, that's why it's called Arise? Note that I said it’s a prequel in nature, which doesn't mean Arise actually connects to SAC, the '95 version, or the manga. It’s just another independent new version. Arise's Motoko is all about being young; she’s not as calm or composed as the previous two versions, and she’s more impulsive and prone to snapping. For the first time ever, Motoko actually feels like a young girl , which is genuinely quite refreshing. Another point that must be mentioned is. definitely the voice cast. That’s right, the entire cast for this one has been swapped out! The Major changed from Atsuko Tanaka to Maaya Sakamoto, who has voiced a younger Motoko more than once before, so casting her makes perfect sense. As for the result, the reception for this work was actually quite polarized. Some didn't like this version’s world-building; despite being a prequel, the scenery looks more modern than any other installment— it’s a very clean and tidy Tokyo. Others disliked how the movie changed the Major’s origin, shifting from.

someone who gradually replaced their body parts to someone who never had a human body at all, having been placed in a mechanical shell from birth. This effectively eliminates the philosophical inquiry that allowed the original '95 version to become a classic. Would you say it’s very bad? It’s not exactly terrible, but it just feels mediocre. It happens to align with my personal feelings about another series from I.G that changed writers midway through—it’s not a very pleasant experience. DreamWorks. bought the adaptation rights for Ghost in the Shell in 2008, and after nearly nine years, they finally produced this Hollywood live-action version, starring the very familiar Scarlett Johansson. The positioning of this film is a bit strange. For one, its blueprint is undoubtedly the original 1995 version, with a bunch of shots in the film recreated exactly like the animation, such as the opening attack on the high-level meeting of cyborg-supporters , and surely the famous scene of the Major activating her thermoptic camouflage and falling must be recreated too, right? But it also incorporates elements from SAC and. Arise, though there are still quite a few adaptations you wouldn’t have expected. The biggest difference is that the heroine’s name isn't even Motoko Kusanagi; it’s Mira Killian. Right, a Western name that just happens to have the same initials as Kusanagi Motoko. At the time of the film's promotion, it sparked significant controversy, with everyone outraged: " How could you cast a white person to play the Major?" This is just whitewashing! But you know, I find it quite lacking. It’s precisely because they wanted to clear that point that. they changed the protagonist—I’ll just spoil it, it shouldn’t matter— into a Japanese woman with her brain placed inside a white body. That is Motoko, which turned the film's main plot into an adventure of exploring her origins and searching for memories of her past life. In short, this film is generally considered another live-action adaptation disaster, though not as tragic as Dragonball. The special effects and set design were genuinely quite good. However, the live-action version ultimately turned a sci-fi film that encouraged audiences. to pause and ponder the meaning of existence into something very superficial, and to put it bluntly, a very hollow commercial film. Coming to this version, it's arguably the strangest of the entire series: SAC_2045, commonly known as the 3D version or the Netflix version, co-produced by Production I.G and Sola Digital Arts. Technically, this can be seen as a sequel to Kenji Kamiyama’s Stand Alone Complex, and with a few exceptions, the voice cast remains the same as the previous installment. It is also deeply regrettable that 2045 is.

actually the final version where Ms. Tanaka portrays Motoko. The story. The story takes place 15 years after Stand Alone Complex, in the year 2045, where global economies are currently sustained solely by war. Public Security Section 9 has since been disbanded, and Motoko and her team have become mercenaries carrying out missions everywhere. Well, the defining feature of 2045 is written all over its face: it's produced entirely in 3D. Needless to say, its announcement. sparked a wave of backlash, and to be honest, the visuals are indeed not ideal. I know it sounds strange to say this about a series where half the main cast are cyborgs. The character models in 2045 look just too artificial, too lacking in humanity. Looking at these plastic figures, it’s hard to feel immersed, especially since Ghost in the Shell is a series known for its detailed and slightly grotesque mechanical internal structures. Characters are always losing limbs or heads, revealing the parts and wires inside, you know? It’s very difficult. to achieve that effect using CG. However, being in 3D space, this entry does have quite a few camera movements that feel like a big-budget Hollywood blockbuster, along with explosions and gunfire. You could say that is the biggest and only advantage of 2045. But I actually feel that it's precisely because they have been trying to cater to modern trends over the past few years that their later works have become increasingly less appealing. Also, we need to remember that Ghost in the Shell became a sci-fi classic back in the 80s, a time when the general public didn't even fully grasp the concept of wireless internet, yet it. introduced the ideas of digitizing the human body and archiving the human brain. Yeah, looking at it through today's lens, the Major and her team live in 2029 and 2030, but they still need to plug in wires to transfer files —it’s totally backward. Where’s your Wi-Fi or AirDrop? That’s why versions like Arise and 2045 try to bring the tech level up to modern standards, adding tablets, smartphones, cryptocurrency, AI, big data, and all sorts of other new gadgets. However, by doing this, the identity that. originally belonged to Ghost in the Shell has slowly faded away. So, having reached this point, the series only has one path left to take. Yes, arriving at this year's latest version, produced by the bold Science SARU, Ghost in the Shell 2026 takes on a rather domineering title, simply called "The Ghost in the Shell," signaling that it is the one and only authentic version. It may seem arrogant, but it's reasonable; as the series has spanned.

31 years, who would have thought this is the only version faithful to the original work? Did I mention that earlier? The Motoko Kusanagi from the original manga and the Motoko portrayed by Mamoru Oshii are practically two different people. OK, now you know how big the gap really is, right? The new Major is super cute, her expressions are so rich it kills me, and this is the feeling she really gave off in the manga. The story's tone also sweeps away the hard-boiled seriousness of all previous versions, becoming incredibly lighthearted, and it doesn't hold back when it needs to be racy either. Whether intentional or not, the "yuri" trend that's been so hot lately—they were already doing it 37 years ago. They were truly ahead of their time. The crows in the animation look like they hopped straight out of something like "Modern Toss," and later on, there's even a gag where a crow’s feathers get blown away, turning it into a hairless bird. The Tachikomas even grow mouths at times, showcasing all sorts of cartoonish expressions that fit the style perfectly; honestly, that’s one of my favorite things about this new version. Of course, they aren't just fooling around the whole. time; they know when to get serious, attempting to find a balance between depth and cuteness. For example, there’s a garbage man who is discovered by Section 9 to have been hacked long-term, with false memories implanted in his brain to make him think he had a wife and kids. This trait is key in the original work, included in both the Oshii version and the new version. You can clearly see Oshii trying hard to emphasize, "My god , can memories actually be tampered with?" He does his absolute best to portray that feeling of, "Is my entire. life fake?" The sense of frustration and despair is there, but the new version adopts a tone closer to the manga, expressing a more helpless resignation, though you can still feel that subtle...reality. Presence is something this work focuses on. Saying goodbye to the modern scenery of earlier entries, the new version thoroughly restores the future world as envisioned by Masamune Shirow back in 1989 when the manga was created. The main setting of the story returns to. the chaotic underbelly of the city. Of course, the technology is still sci-fi, but you can see those messy cables and the bizarre yet truly cool internal mechanical structures have made a comeback. Look, this sharp, high-tech blazer and the tree-like interface are both retro and trendy. They look amazing. Right, the voice actor is Maaya Sakamoto, just like in Arise. This is the first Ghost in the Shell release since Ms. Tanaka's passing, and fortunately, the series already had the.

perfect successor lined up. As an aside , Akio Otsuka, who plays Batou, posted a very touching tribute on Twitter after Ms. Tanaka's passing. Ah. Alright , that was a brief introduction to the various versions of Ghost in the Shell. I'm Jing Chuan Yi. I know there would be more if we included the manga and games, but I think these six animated series and films are the core works of the franchise. Which version is your favorite? Feel free to share in the. comments. I'm Jing Chuan Yi, and my personal favorite has to be the latest 2026 version. The situation with Ghost in the Shell, compared to Doraemon, Conan, or Crayon Shin-chan, I think is actually more like Batman. Right, in the realm of American comics, Batman is undoubtedly one of the biggest figures with the widest range of styles. From the super serious, grounded versions like Bale's or Pattinson's, to the hilariously campy Adam West version, and even the Lego version. The point is , all these Batmans are equally recognized, which, when you think about. it, is truly no simple feat. Ghost in the Shell and Motoko Kusanagi are in a similar situation for me. Also, don't miss the collab between Girl Cafe Gun and Ghost in the Shell: SAC_2045; the link is below, so join now to take home these adorable chibi versions of the Major! I'm Jingchuan, see you in the next video.

actually the final version where Ms. Tanaka portrays Motoko. The story. It may seem arrogant, but it's reasonable; as the series has spanned.

31 years, who would have thought this is the only version faithful to the original work? Did I mention that earlier? The Motoko Kusanagi from the original manga and the Motoko portrayed by Mamoru Oshii are practically two different people. OK, now you know how big the gap really is, right? The new Major is super cute, her expressions are so rich it kills me, and this is the feeling she really gave off in the manga. The story's tone also sweeps away the hard-boiled seriousness of all previous versions, becoming incredibly lighthearted, and it doesn't hold back when it needs to be racy either. Whether intentional or not, the "yuri" trend that's been so hot lately—they were already doing it 37 years ago. They were truly ahead of their time. The crows in the animation look like they hopped straight out of something like "Modern Toss," and later on, there's even a gag where a crow’s feathers get blown away, turning it into a hairless bird. The Tachikomas even grow mouths at times, showcasing all sorts of cartoonish expressions that fit the style perfectly; honestly, that’s one of my favorite things about this new version. Of course, they aren't just fooling around the whole. time; they know when to get serious, attempting to find a balance between depth and cuteness. For example, there’s a garbage man who is discovered by Section 9 to have been hacked long-term, with false memories implanted in his brain to make him think he had a wife and kids. This trait is key in the original work, included in both the Oshii version and the new version. You can clearly see Oshii trying hard to emphasize, "My god , can memories actually be tampered with?" He does his absolute best to portray that feeling of, "Is my entire. life fake?" The sense of frustration and despair is there, but the new version adopts a tone closer to the manga, expressing a more helpless resignation, though you can still feel that subtle...reality. Presence is something this work focuses on. Saying goodbye to the modern scenery of earlier entries, the new version thoroughly restores the future world as envisioned by Masamune Shirow back in 1989 when the manga was created. The main setting of the story returns to. the chaotic underbelly of the city. Of course, the technology is still sci-fi, but you can see those messy cables and the bizarre yet truly cool internal mechanical structures have made a comeback. Look, this sharp, high-tech blazer and the tree-like interface are both retro and trendy. They look amazing. Right, the voice actor is Maaya Sakamoto, just like in Arise. perfect successor lined up. As an aside , Akio Otsuka, who plays Batou, posted a very touching tribute on Twitter after Ms. Tanaka's passing. Ah. Right, in the realm of American comics, Batman is undoubtedly one of the biggest figures with the widest range of styles. The point is , all these Batmans are equally recognized, which, when you think about. it, is truly no simple feat. Ghost in the Shell and Motoko Kusanagi are in a similar situation for me. I'm Jingchuan, see you in the next video.

No matter how this IP evolves, this baseline remains constant. In 1995, 31 years ago, Ghost in the Shell got its first animation adaptation, turned into a film by Production I.G. The title was. very simple: "Ghost in the Shell," and it was, of course, directed by Mamoru Oshii. To this day, this version remains the main impression the general public has of the series—cold, serious, and philosophical. It is largely one of the pioneers of today's popular cyberpunk worldview. Wait, if it's not Ghost in the Shell, then it's Blade Runner, right? Blade Runner provided that messy, rain-soaked, Asian-inspired aesthetic filled with neon signs, while Ghost in the Shell did more to popularize the concept of human body modification. Yes, so. without Ghost in the Shell, there would be no Cyberpunk 2077, okay? A big focus of this film is that the Major's body is almost entirely replaced by machine parts. She feels very cold and distant, prioritizing her missions above all else, just like a robot. Those who know a bit about the original work should know this is a huge departure from it, right? We will discuss this later, but this change serves to emphasize the core theme the film explores: once your.

entire body is no longer made of flesh, what exactly is it that keeps you human ? In a world where even memories can be fabricated, how can you be sure you are the person who has truly lived your life, rather than a replica whose data was uploaded just yesterday? If you grasp the message the film intends to convey, you will understand why this work is titled "Ghost in the Shell." Your body is ultimately just a shell; what truly matters is the consciousness , the "Ghost," inside. As long as it remains, it is the greatest proof that you are alive. In short, the 1995 Mamoru Oshii version is undoubtedly a cinematic masterpiece. Hollywood blockbusters like The Matrix were clearly deeply influenced by this film, and many scenes later became iconic moments that successors vied to pay homage to. Especially that most classic scene of the Major activating her thermoptic camouflage and slowly descending—future adaptations always. find a way to recreate it when given the chance! The incredibly detailed mechanical gunfight animation and the painstakingly hand-drawn mechanical movements remain, even today, a form of unparalleled, exquisite art. Following the massive success of the '95 Oshii version, I.G immediately threw themselves into the production of the sequel, Innocence. But as fans know, the production of Innocence was severely delayed, the budget ballooned, and worst of all, it flopped at the box office after its release. Back then,. the entire Production I.G company nearly went bankrupt, so while waiting for Innocence, I.G decided to develop another animated version of Ghost in the Shell. Little did they know they would create a classic to rival the films: Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex, directed by Kenji Kamiyama. The overall feel of SAC is as if it sits right between Oshii’s version and Masamune Shirow’s original manga. It isn't as somber as the films, nor as lighthearted as the manga; watching it feels like a sci-fi action series with. a very American TV show vibe. The title reflects the show's format— "Stand Alone Complex"—but what does that mean? "Stand Alone" refers to simple, standalone cases that conclude in a single episode, while "Complex" refers to the larger, main story arcs that require multiple episodes to unfold. Now, speaking of the Major in SAC, although she is still voiced by Atsuko Tanaka, her performance feels much more "human," no longer just a half-human, half-machine cyborg exploring the.

boundaries of humanity. This version of the Major is a confident, cool, and sexy queen. Motoko Kusanagi's outfits are eye-catching, and there are even some scenes that are super explicit with fan service. Anyway, enough about that. When it comes to Stand Alone Complex, I think its most important contribution is giving every member of Public Security Section 9 a chance to be known and loved by the audience. If you only watch the movie version,. it’s easy to get the impression that only Motoko and Batou really matter. But in SAC, you get the Major’s boss Aramaki, the least augmented and most " human" Togusa, plus Ishikawa, Saito, Borma, Pazu, and the others. And among them, the most important are certainly the Tachikomas. That’s right, these little tanks that look like hermit crabs were cut from the movie to maintain its tone, but they are absolutely the series 'mascots, even if their names were changed to Tachikoma. for various corporate reasons and their color turned blue. In short, I would say Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex was a career-defining work for Production I.G, because where did I.G's different production lines and I.G. Sixth Division come from? That's right, Ghost in the Shell. The most famous among them is none other than I.G. Sixth Division, which handled the best works and later became the powerhouse WIT Studio. Futuristic sci-fi police thrillers like this one became the main. impression of I.G for a very long time. For instance, Psycho-Pass was clearly inspired by SAC, at least until they realized how profitable "pretty boys" are. Now, we can also meet the Major in the world of Tower of Fantasy! This Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex collaboration officially begins on October 28th. Tower of Fantasy itself has a bit of a cyberpunk world-building style, so this collaboration with Ghost in the Shell is a perfect match. It adds a brand new collab pet Tachikoma,. "Motoko," as well as a collab vehicle, the Tachikoma, and five different paint jobs. My favorite is this heavier armored version. SYNCED is an incredibly satisfying multiplayer co-op action game. This collaboration even features an exclusive four-player mode for Ghost in the Shell—it's brilliant ! You and your friends can pilot Tachikomas, shooting, gathering resources, and upgrading while you compete. It’s absolutely a blast. The Halloween event "Phantom Night" is making a strong return. Collect puzzles , challenge bosses, and explore mysterious pumpkins—there's so much fun festive content waiting for you to discover. The level cap has been raised to 80! Once you break through this.

threshold, the game prepares a brand-new adventure chapter, " Redemption Sanctum," and a new map, " The Sanctum," where the long-awaited antagonist Conrad finally makes an appearance. In short, this Ghost in the Shell collaboration update is definitely not just about adding a few pets or vehicles; it’s a comprehensive major upgrade with new storylines, new dungeons, and new explorable areas. There's also the new Pilgrim gear, so it doesn't matter if you haven't played SYNCED for a while. The returning player event helps adventurers catch up to the top tier in an instant. Returning players can use the level-boost perk to reach a maxed-out state at level 70, so you can. join everyone else and push to level 80 immediately. Plus, by staying active for seven consecutive days, you can claim high-tier gear and various custom resource bundles, making catching up completely stress-free. Whether you’re a total newbie or a seasoned veteran, now is the perfect time to jump in or return. Entering the 2010s, Production I.G successfully developed several new hits, and it felt like Ghost in the Shell's mission had reached a temporary conclusion. That was until 2013's Ghost in the Shell: Arise, directed by Kazuchika Kise. This. version...well, as you can all tell, its biggest label is that the art style is essentially "Naruto." Yes, the character designs were by Takayuki Takadera. This naturally caused some dissatisfaction among old-school fans, but looking at Naruto in 2026, he doesn't even look like the original anymore—more like Kaiju No. 8—so it doesn't seem that bad now, right? This is a theatrical series spanning five works, with a different positioning than before. It leans toward a prequel, telling the story of Motoko Kusanagi. during her military days before joining Public Security Section 9. So, that's why it's called Arise? Note that I said it’s a prequel in nature, which doesn't mean Arise actually connects to SAC, the '95 version, or the manga. It’s just another independent new version. Arise's Motoko is all about being young; she’s not as calm or composed as the previous two versions, and she’s more impulsive and prone to snapping. For the first time ever, Motoko actually feels like a young girl , which is genuinely quite refreshing. Another point that must be mentioned is. definitely the voice cast. That’s right, the entire cast for this one has been swapped out! The Major changed from Atsuko Tanaka to Maaya Sakamoto, who has voiced a younger Motoko more than once before, so casting her makes perfect sense. As for the result, the reception for this work was actually quite polarized. Some didn't like this version’s world-building; despite being a prequel, the scenery looks more modern than any other installment— it’s a very clean and tidy Tokyo. Others disliked how the movie changed the Major’s origin, shifting from.

someone who gradually replaced their body parts to someone who never had a human body at all, having been placed in a mechanical shell from birth. This effectively eliminates the philosophical inquiry that allowed the original '95 version to become a classic. Would you say it’s very bad? It’s not exactly terrible, but it just feels mediocre. It happens to align with my personal feelings about another series from I.G that changed writers midway through—it’s not a very pleasant experience. DreamWorks. bought the adaptation rights for Ghost in the Shell in 2008, and after nearly nine years, they finally produced this Hollywood live-action version, starring the very familiar Scarlett Johansson. The positioning of this film is a bit strange. For one, its blueprint is undoubtedly the original 1995 version, with a bunch of shots in the film recreated exactly like the animation, such as the opening attack on the high-level meeting of cyborg-supporters , and surely the famous scene of the Major activating her thermoptic camouflage and falling must be recreated too, right? But it also incorporates elements from SAC and. Arise, though there are still quite a few adaptations you wouldn’t have expected. The biggest difference is that the heroine’s name isn't even Motoko Kusanagi; it’s Mira Killian. Right, a Western name that just happens to have the same initials as Kusanagi Motoko. At the time of the film's promotion, it sparked significant controversy, with everyone outraged: " How could you cast a white person to play the Major?" This is just whitewashing! But you know, I find it quite lacking. It’s precisely because they wanted to clear that point that. they changed the protagonist—I’ll just spoil it, it shouldn’t matter— into a Japanese woman with her brain placed inside a white body. That is Motoko, which turned the film's main plot into an adventure of exploring her origins and searching for memories of her past life. In short, this film is generally considered another live-action adaptation disaster, though not as tragic as Dragonball. The special effects and set design were genuinely quite good. However, the live-action version ultimately turned a sci-fi film that encouraged audiences. to pause and ponder the meaning of existence into something very superficial, and to put it bluntly, a very hollow commercial film. Coming to this version, it's arguably the strangest of the entire series: SAC_2045, commonly known as the 3D version or the Netflix version, co-produced by Production I.G and Sola Digital Arts. Technically, this can be seen as a sequel to Kenji Kamiyama’s Stand Alone Complex, and with a few exceptions, the voice cast remains the same as the previous installment. It is also deeply regrettable that 2045 is.

actually the final version where Ms. Tanaka portrays Motoko. The story. The story takes place 15 years after Stand Alone Complex, in the year 2045, where global economies are currently sustained solely by war. Public Security Section 9 has since been disbanded, and Motoko and her team have become mercenaries carrying out missions everywhere. Well, the defining feature of 2045 is written all over its face: it's produced entirely in 3D. Needless to say, its announcement. sparked a wave of backlash, and to be honest, the visuals are indeed not ideal. I know it sounds strange to say this about a series where half the main cast are cyborgs. The character models in 2045 look just too artificial, too lacking in humanity. Looking at these plastic figures, it’s hard to feel immersed, especially since Ghost in the Shell is a series known for its detailed and slightly grotesque mechanical internal structures. Characters are always losing limbs or heads, revealing the parts and wires inside, you know? It’s very difficult. to achieve that effect using CG. However, being in 3D space, this entry does have quite a few camera movements that feel like a big-budget Hollywood blockbuster, along with explosions and gunfire. You could say that is the biggest and only advantage of 2045. But I actually feel that it's precisely because they have been trying to cater to modern trends over the past few years that their later works have become increasingly less appealing. Also, we need to remember that Ghost in the Shell became a sci-fi classic back in the 80s, a time when the general public didn't even fully grasp the concept of wireless internet, yet it. introduced the ideas of digitizing the human body and archiving the human brain. Yeah, looking at it through today's lens, the Major and her team live in 2029 and 2030, but they still need to plug in wires to transfer files —it’s totally backward. Where’s your Wi-Fi or AirDrop? That’s why versions like Arise and 2045 try to bring the tech level up to modern standards, adding tablets, smartphones, cryptocurrency, AI, big data, and all sorts of other new gadgets. However, by doing this, the identity that. originally belonged to Ghost in the Shell has slowly faded away. So, having reached this point, the series only has one path left to take. Yes, arriving at this year's latest version, produced by the bold Science SARU, Ghost in the Shell 2026 takes on a rather domineering title, simply called "The Ghost in the Shell," signaling that it is the one and only authentic version. It may seem arrogant, but it's reasonable; as the series has spanned.

31 years, who would have thought this is the only version faithful to the original work? Did I mention that earlier? The Motoko Kusanagi from the original manga and the Motoko portrayed by Mamoru Oshii are practically two different people. OK, now you know how big the gap really is, right? The new Major is super cute, her expressions are so rich it kills me, and this is the feeling she really gave off in the manga. The story's tone also sweeps away the hard-boiled seriousness of all previous versions, becoming incredibly lighthearted, and it doesn't hold back when it needs to be racy either. Whether intentional or not, the "yuri" trend that's been so hot lately—they were already doing it 37 years ago. They were truly ahead of their time. The crows in the animation look like they hopped straight out of something like "Modern Toss," and later on, there's even a gag where a crow’s feathers get blown away, turning it into a hairless bird. The Tachikomas even grow mouths at times, showcasing all sorts of cartoonish expressions that fit the style perfectly; honestly, that’s one of my favorite things about this new version. Of course, they aren't just fooling around the whole. time; they know when to get serious, attempting to find a balance between depth and cuteness. For example, there’s a garbage man who is discovered by Section 9 to have been hacked long-term, with false memories implanted in his brain to make him think he had a wife and kids. This trait is key in the original work, included in both the Oshii version and the new version. You can clearly see Oshii trying hard to emphasize, "My god , can memories actually be tampered with?" He does his absolute best to portray that feeling of, "Is my entire. life fake?" The sense of frustration and despair is there, but the new version adopts a tone closer to the manga, expressing a more helpless resignation, though you can still feel that subtle...reality. Presence is something this work focuses on. Saying goodbye to the modern scenery of earlier entries, the new version thoroughly restores the future world as envisioned by Masamune Shirow back in 1989 when the manga was created. The main setting of the story returns to. the chaotic underbelly of the city. Of course, the technology is still sci-fi, but you can see those messy cables and the bizarre yet truly cool internal mechanical structures have made a comeback. Look, this sharp, high-tech blazer and the tree-like interface are both retro and trendy. They look amazing. Right, the voice actor is Maaya Sakamoto, just like in Arise. This is the first Ghost in the Shell release since Ms. Tanaka's passing, and fortunately, the series already had the.

perfect successor lined up. As an aside , Akio Otsuka, who plays Batou, posted a very touching tribute on Twitter after Ms. Tanaka's passing. Ah. Alright , that was a brief introduction to the various versions of Ghost in the Shell. I'm Jing Chuan Yi. I know there would be more if we included the manga and games, but I think these six animated series and films are the core works of the franchise. Which version is your favorite? Feel free to share in the. comments. I'm Jing Chuan Yi, and my personal favorite has to be the latest 2026 version. The situation with Ghost in the Shell, compared to Doraemon, Conan, or Crayon Shin-chan, I think is actually more like Batman. Right, in the realm of American comics, Batman is undoubtedly one of the biggest figures with the widest range of styles. From the super serious, grounded versions like Bale's or Pattinson's, to the hilariously campy Adam West version, and even the Lego version. The point is , all these Batmans are equally recognized, which, when you think about. it, is truly no simple feat. Ghost in the Shell and Motoko Kusanagi are in a similar situation for me. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析《火影忍者》與《博人傳》主角評價兩極的核心心理與敘事差異。
  • 客觀拆解鳴人與博人父子間不同的成長背景、叛逆動機及觀眾的情感投射。
  • 探討王道少年漫畫中「底層逆襲」與「天才神童」設定對觀眾共鳴的深遠影響。

摘要

探討《博人傳》風評的真實現象

作者指出，儘管全球動漫迷對《火影忍者》懷有深厚情感，續作《博人傳》卻長期承受巨大爭議。作者澄清自己並非單純為了跟風抹黑，雖然承認《博人傳》水準確實不如前作，但當前網路上許多人僅是將其當作流行爛梗來嘲弄。作者希望跳脫盲從情緒，客觀剖析觀眾為何始終無法像喜愛鳴人那樣接納博人，究竟是劇情編排出了問題，還是博人的性格本身就不討喜。

出身背景與情感投射的巨大落差

作者分析，兩位主角在成長起點上有著極大反差。漩渦鳴人是極致的「草根逆襲」代表，童年孤苦無依、受盡全村冷落，這種底層奮鬥的經歷極易引發觀眾的同情與支持。相反地，漩渦博人身為火影之子，含著金湯匙出生且生活富足，容易被貼上「不知民間疾苦的富二代」標籤。當博人展現青春期叛逆時，一路伴隨鳴人成長的觀眾往往會以長輩立場斥責其不知感恩，導致兩者在觀眾緣上產生天壤之別。

行為動機與天才人設帶來的共鳴斷層

作者進一步對比兩人的塗鴉惡作劇：鳴人是為了被大家看見而擺脫孤立，博人則是源於父親長期缺席家庭、甚至以影分身參加妹妹生日所引發的情感失衡。雖然博人愛護妹妹的心態為他減輕了負面形象，但在天賦上，博人卻是個思維敏捷、一點就通的天才少年。不同於鳴人經歷無數挫折才習得忍術的刻苦過程，博人輕易掌握強大忍術的設定，反而削弱了傳統王道少年漫畫中最具渲染力的奮鬥共鳴。

This is Naruto, one of the most beloved manga in the world. This is Boruto: Naruto Next Generations, one of the most hated manga in the world. Why do people love Naruto but hate Boruto? Hi everyone , I'm Jingchuan Yi. Naruto has been teasing a new series since 2023, and recently we finally got some news, with Kishimoto even announcing a new serialization. Many Naruto fans saw this and exclaimed, "Does this mean we finally don't have to watch Boruto anymore?" It’s like they’ve forgotten that the Boruto anime ended four years. ago, and would it even continue if the story wasn't good? Regardless, this makes me want to discuss an age-old question: Why can't Naruto fans like Boruto the same way they liked Naruto? Is it a problem with the plot, or is it that Boruto's personality itself is just unlikable? Today, I want to share some of my own thoughts on this. OK, if you enjoy this video, feel free to check out my recent videos on "The Most Questionable Settings in Anime" and " The Real Gap Between Aizen and Sosuke." Likes, subscriptions, and Super Thanks. are all greatly appreciated. Before we start, there are two points I need to clarify, otherwise I’m afraid you might misunderstand my stance. First , this is not the 101st video on the internet bashing Boruto. At this point, there's no need for me to do that. If you came here expecting me to trash Boruto, sorry, you’re going to be disappointed. Second, if you ask me whether I prefer "Naruto" or "Boruto," of course I think "Naruto" is better, okay? Right, please don’t misunderstand. . I admit that Boruto is mostly not very good; that’s an indisputable fact. But, and this is a big but, I feel that 80% of people these days aren't criticizing Boruto for legitimate reasons, they’re just hating on it to follow the trend, you know? They use Boruto as a convenient punchline. Whenever they want to compare something to garbage, they just throw out the name Boruto, and it always works. That’s what I mean. Alright, so are Naruto Uzumaki and Boruto Uzumaki—parenthetically, Bolt—a father and son? Duh, who doesn't know. that? The two share some very similar baselines, for instance, their appearance goes without saying—they are very much alike, he Naruto loves eating at Ichiraku Ramen, while Boruto loves grabbing burgers at Thunder Burger, and they even like the same size. Father and son have plenty in common, but apart from that, their upbringing and natural talent have created two protagonists: one who has been beloved from the start, and another who was criticized from day one. First, a common point people criticize Boruto. for is that he has it too easy. His mom is from a prominent clan in the village , and his dad is the greatest Hokage. He lives in a big house and enjoys a wealthy lifestyle; he’s essentially that classic "second-generation" rich kid who’s out of touch with reality, right? In contrast, look at how much his dad suffered when he was young. A kid living alone, eating instant noodles and drinking expired milk every day. Most importantly, because of the Nine-Tails, Naruto was ostracized, had no friends, and grew up all by himself. Looking at it this way, it’s clear which one.

resonates more with the audience. And I have to say, Naruto is, by nature, one of the most classic underdog stories in the world of shonen manga. Take stories like Cinderella, Harry Potter, or Cyberpunk: Edgerunners; they’re all the same. Watching the protagonist climb up from being a nobody to eventually reaching the summit—these "rags to riches" or "ugly duckling" stories are the easiest to connect with. Audiences immediately root for the protagonist. But Boruto has it tougher; he had his footing pulled out from under him right. from the start. After all, you can’t just destroy the protagonists’ happy ending right out of the gate, can you? That’s why Boruto had to start by creating a sense of suspense: the Hidden Leaf Village in ruins, a scar over his eye, and the claim that the age of the ninja is over. It throws the future at us right away to spark curiosity and keep us reading. Furthermore, Boruto has to be extra careful with his actions because he was born with a silver spoon in his mouth. Even slightly showing the immaturity or. impulsiveness typical of a teenager at his age can be risky. He might get scolded with things like, "You kids nowadays have no idea how hard your parents had it back then! You just know how to be rebellious all day, even throwing your dad's clothes out; you're just plain ungrateful!" Wow, why does that tone sound so familiar? Ha, there is one thing that I think clearly highlights the difference in how Naruto and Boruto are perceived due to their different backgrounds. Both Naruto and Boruto have climbed up to the Hokage faces to graffiti them. Nobody had any issue when Naruto did it, because at the. time, the audience didn't have any other perspective to consider. We all empathized with Naruto, thinking he was hated by the whole village and felt so sorry for him, so a little prank didn't seem to matter. However, it's a different story with Boruto. By the time of Boruto's generation, the audience had spent years following Naruto's perspective. The reasons for Naruto and Boruto's pranks are actually quite different. For one, it's a desire to be seen by everyone; even if most villagers dislike him, it's still better than being treated like air. For the other, it stems from an emotional imbalance due to a lack of fatherly attention. His dad is busy with work all day and refuses to come home, so this is the only way to get him to show up. To sum it up, I think Kishimoto and his team really tried hard to push Boruto into that "ungrateful brat" trap, and they succeeded in making him. sufficiently annoying. It's like, "Hey, Dad, it's fine if you don't care about me, whatever." He’s kind of given up on himself, but surely you should at least properly participate in your sister's childhood, right? What really makes Boruto angry is that Naruto even sent a Shadow Clone to Himawari's birthday. That was undeniably Naruto's fault, and no audience member can criticize Boruto for that. During the cheating exam, didn't Naruto just give up right away? But if it were Boruto, I guarantee he would have solved the problems directly , you know? He just catches on to everything instantly. Naruto spent forever popping water balloons to learn the Rasengan, but Boruto mastered it in half the time . On top of that, he could fluently combine Shadow Clones with Wind, Lightning, and Water Style jutsu, and.

even summoning techniques, right from the start. And he’s got natural charisma , too! I mean, honestly, with Naruto’s outgoing personality, if it weren’t for the Nine-Tails holding him back, his social life wouldn't have been that bad , would it? Boruto never had that burden , so he immediately became the center of attention in class. Of course, that makes some people unhappy, complaining, "Boruto is such a Gary Stu. He doesn’t have to try at all, everything is just handed to him. This protagonist is totally unlikeable." Though, I have to ask: since when did a protagonist's. intelligence start determining how likeable they are? If you want to go there, didn't Joseph Joestar master Hamon on his own right from the start? And the ultimate move that killed Jonathan was easily countered by Joseph with just a glass! How come I never heard Jojo fans complaining, "Ugh, that's unfair, Joseph sucks"? Well, there are many reasons. First off, Part 2 is way more popular than Part 1, that's one thing. Plus, Joseph's personality is just so incredibly distinct. In comparison, Boruto doesn't have as strong of a personality, and I. agree with that; that is a fact. But speaking solely on talent, I still want to defend Boruto a little. First, even though he's Naruto's son, you can't forget that half his bloodline comes from the Hyuga clan. Do you really think a child of the Hyuga family would be that dull? Second, I actually don't think Naruto was ever that stupid. Looking back, the reason for his poor grades early on was likely because he lacked a fundamental element for growth. during his studies. What was it? It was peers. Everyone who’s been to school knows that when you have questions and no classmates to ask, it really affects your understanding of the material, right? I won't even talk about Shippuden ; just look at the Chunin Exams. Naruto defeated opponents many times through sheer flashes of brilliance. For example , against Neji, he used a feint to catch him off guard, and he even copied Sasuke's Lion Combo on the spot, adapting it into his own "Naruto Uzumaki Barrage." Naruto had those kinds of. instant-learn techniques too, but only Boruto gets put under this kind of microscope. You know, one of the few highlights of the combat in Boruto is seeing him rely purely on his intellect to combine standard techniques and find a way to win. Unlike Naruto; throughout his main series, his protagonist presence was always so strong that he never used the ordinary moves other characters did, relying only on Shadow Clones, Rasengan, Sage Mode, or Tailed Beast Chakra—those exclusive main-character moves. If you wanted to see Naruto use a normal Earth Style wall. , where would you even look? Exactly, you'd only see that in Boruto. Of course , later on, once Boruto unlocked "Karma ," those merits started to fade away; it’s true, you could argue this is one of the very few benefits of the Boruto anime's progress being so heavily stifled by the manga. Regardless, Boruto spent a long time overcoming the shortcoming of his main-character power-up not showing up until nearly 100 episodes in by relying on his wits and teamwork. The best example, I think, is the bell.

test with Kakashi; if you recall, Team 7 took that test and essentially passed by luck because Sasuke and Sakura didn't abandon Naruto, but Boruto grasped the true purpose of that test right away: it was meant to see if they understood teamwork. Because of that, the whole class centered their strategy around Boruto and came up with a brilliant tactic, coming within a hair's breadth of grabbing the bell, and the result, of course, was that everyone passed. I never disliked Boruto from the very. beginning. When he faced Kawaki in the manga and didn't hesitate for a second to hold a shuriken to his own neck, I quite liked him when he first appeared in the anime. Now that the manga has reached this point, I finally understand the level of resolve Boruto had when he said, "Even so, I'm still a ninja," in the first episode. Naruto endured the cold glares of his villagers growing up , while Boruto has endured the cold glares of netizens; the scale of this is simply incomparable. It’s an undeniable fact that second-generation characters are easily put under scrutiny, both in reality and fiction, but the reason. Boruto is so disliked, and its protagonist so resented, is that the creators give off the feeling of forcefully extending the story and milking an old IP. Okay, so listening up to this point, you should be able to tell that I've been defending Boruto the protagonist pretty hard. Because for me , the reason Boruto isn't good isn't that the protagonist is unlikable; it's that the stories happening around him are just hard to describe, and Boruto is just a victim of circumstance. What is Boruto most criticized for? Forcibly nerfing characters, an overly sci-fi. world, fighting aliens, power creep, time travel, and later on, things like battleships and light arrows. Coming up with all this random stuff isn't Boruto's fault; the aliens were something the original series brought in anyway. But speaking of this, people might play their trump card. What is it? Exactly, the biggest issue most people have with Boruto is that his character arc is hard to resonate with. Just comparing him to what his dad did in the past, there’s a huge problem— especially cheating on the exam, the difference is just too vast. When Boruto took the Chunin Exams, he actually cheated using scientific ninja tools, and ended up getting caught by his dad and scolded publicly, being told he was "not qualified to be a ninja." This one incident alone has made many Boruto-haters chase him for over a decade now; they still haven't let it go . Of course, you might ask, was Boruto cheating on the exam his fault? Yes, it 100%was, there’s no denying that. But. he’s just a teenager; is having a little opportunistic mindset really that serious? I mean, who hasn't felt anxious about their own lack of strength when they were young and wanted to take a shortcut? Plus, I think Boruto must have been afraid that if he didn't perform well enough or got eliminated, he'd be scrutinized and told, "Like father, like son; you're nothing compared to your great father." The important thing is learning and growing from mistakes, but Boruto isn't allowed to have any human flaws, or the typical recklessness that comes with.

that age. And the reason for that is simply because he is the son of Naruto Uzumaki . Wow, doesn't it feel like the fiction and reality just connected? See what I mean? Boruto does have a halo, sure, but his hardest struggle is that everyone only sees the brightness of that halo. I never thought about this. And at this point, you add in the issues with how the anime was adapted. Let me briefly explain for those who aren't familiar: "Boruto can't get hyped" is. probably the most common criticism you hear about this series, but why exactly can't it get hyped? The reason is that the production speeds for this series ' anime and manga are just too far apart. Normally, an anime should slowly adapt according to the original serialization , right? In the past, one episode of the Naruto anime would consume about one to three weeks of manga progress. However, the biggest problem with the Boruto manga is that it's a monthly release— only one chapter a month—yet the anime puts out four episodes a month. This meant that the Boruto anime was destined to have a massive amount of filler from the start. Those who have watched Naruto or Bleach know very well how insufferable the filler arcs can be. Well, now that about sixty percent of Boruto is filler, I have to note that these filler arcs are actually genuinely pretty good. There are many; for example , I can name one right now: the original opening of the Boruto anime, which I think blows both the movie and the manga out of the water. I really like that the studio chose to slowly depict their. daily lives at the Ninja Academy, and it's just cute, especially the bickering between Sarada and Boruto—isn't that adorable? The anime added original characters like Denki, Iwabe, and the Class Rep. They integrated so well that I can't imagine Boruto without them, and clearly, Ukyo Kodachi and Masashi Kishimoto agreed, which is why they imported the Class Rep back into the manga, right? There are also episodes like the Parent-Child Day that focus on family warmth, which are all great to watch. So, I must emphasize that the. Boruto anime's original content is definitely not trash through and through . It's just a fact that it's padded with a lot of filler. You have to watch about ten episodes just to find one that's truly good. Why can't Boruto get hyped? This, this is the reason. Just think about it: if you were trying to start a fire, but you were forced to take a five-minute break every two seconds, how could the fire ever catch on? You'd be nothing but a skeleton before the fire even starts, haha. Most of the anime's runtime is just waiting for the manga to reach a certain point—a stalling tactic. . Even if the writers wanted to write something serious, sorry, Boruto, Sarada , and Mitsuki can't get significantly stronger, and they can't achieve any major psychological growth, otherwise it wouldn't connect to the manga later on, would it? In the original Naruto, by episode 90, we were already watching the Konoha trio unleash their summoning jutsus in an epic battle. But in Boruto , by episode 90, the trio was still helping the elderly catch birds. Do you feel the problem here? To be honest, if Boruto had started airing a year later, perhaps it could have been.

like Demon Slayer, Jujutsu Kaisen, or Bleach: TYBW, with tight, well-paced seasons of 12 to 24 episodes. However, the fate of a long-running series with nearly 300 episodes is that the animation quality will inevitably fluctuate, and there will always be moments where it fails. If that happens during a major scene, like someone's death, it just turns into a meme. >> If Boruto's crying face is drawn even slightly off, people will laugh at it forever. Boruto is a very peculiar product in anime history. Due to the strange way different versions dragged each other down, the IP's reputation was terrible from the start. Ironically, the manga's reputation only finally took off after the anime ended. For those who haven't watched it, here's a quick summary: Boruto had his entire life rewritten because Eida used her ability to alter the world's perception, making Kawaki. Naruto's son and Boruto the outsider. In an instant, Boruto lost everything he once had. And in an instant, the readers ' perception of Boruto did a complete 180-degree turn. Pain rushed to put his hand on Boruto's shoulder: "Now your pain far exceeds mine." The later stages of the Boruto manga are actually quite good. At the very least, Boruto truly showed the resolve of a ninja, as well as a willpower not inferior to Naruto or Sasuke, which is worth acknowledging. To summarize: Naruto spent his whole life healing his childhood, while Boruto used. his childhood to heal his whole life. Naruto is the yang to the yin, Boruto is the yin to the yang, but in the end, they should arrive at the same destination. Netizens who say things like that are likely those who have been following the manga. Their resentment toward Boruto has probably long since faded, or they never actually hated it to begin with. Those who are still obsessed with hating Boruto until recently are probably just bitter old fans or pure haters. So perhaps it was always two different groups, and it’s not that they suddenly changed their minds. A while ago, wasn't the Naruto spin-off, Shadow Rising, announced? Then. suddenly, a bunch of people popped out of nowhere asking, "Is the original finally going to kick Boruto out of the canon?" Naruto ended in 2014, and Boruto was always just a dream. When I saw it, a giant "ha" popped into my head. This clearly looks like a story purely meant to fill in the gaps around the time they had kids. Besides, even if the main storyline of Naruto isn't 100%handled by Kishimoto, he still decides the general direction. As for what Boruto is actually about, his path to growth. definitely isn't as straightforward as Naruto's, that's for sure. But as it has developed, I would say this character has finally found a path that belongs uniquely to him. His dad's story is about a boy who had nothing and how he earned everyone's respect, so maybe Boruto's is the reverse: telling the tale of a privileged boy and how he must reclaim everything that belongs to him. As for whether it will turn out bad, well, that's another story entirely. Alright, what are everyone else's thoughts? Feel free to leave a comment and share. I'm.

Jingchuan.

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析《火影忍者》與《博人傳》主角評價兩極的核心心理與敘事差異。
  • 客觀拆解鳴人與博人父子間不同的成長背景、叛逆動機及觀眾的情感投射。
  • 探討王道少年漫畫中「底層逆襲」與「天才神童」設定對觀眾共鳴的深遠影響。

摘要

探討《博人傳》風評的真實現象

作者指出，儘管全球動漫迷對《火影忍者》懷有深厚情感，續作《博人傳》卻長期承受巨大爭議。作者澄清自己並非單純為了跟風抹黑，雖然承認《博人傳》水準確實不如前作，但當前網路上許多人僅是將其當作流行爛梗來嘲弄。作者希望跳脫盲從情緒，客觀剖析觀眾為何始終無法像喜愛鳴人那樣接納博人，究竟是劇情編排出了問題，還是博人的性格本身就不討喜。

出身背景與情感投射的巨大落差

作者分析，兩位主角在成長起點上有著極大反差。漩渦鳴人是極致的「草根逆襲」代表，童年孤苦無依、受盡全村冷落，這種底層奮鬥的經歷極易引發觀眾的同情與支持。相反地，漩渦博人身為火影之子，含著金湯匙出生且生活富足，容易被貼上「不知民間疾苦的富二代」標籤。當博人展現青春期叛逆時，一路伴隨鳴人成長的觀眾往往會以長輩立場斥責其不知感恩，導致兩者在觀眾緣上產生天壤之別。

行為動機與天才人設帶來的共鳴斷層

作者進一步對比兩人的塗鴉惡作劇：鳴人是為了被大家看見而擺脫孤立，博人則是源於父親長期缺席家庭、甚至以影分身參加妹妹生日所引發的情感失衡。雖然博人愛護妹妹的心態為他減輕了負面形象，但在天賦上，博人卻是個思維敏捷、一點就通的天才少年。不同於鳴人經歷無數挫折才習得忍術的刻苦過程，博人輕易掌握強大忍術的設定，反而削弱了傳統王道少年漫畫中最具渲染力的奮鬥共鳴。

If you wanted to see Naruto use a normal Earth Style wall. , where would you even look? Exactly, you'd only see that in Boruto. Of course , later on, once Boruto unlocked "Karma ," those merits started to fade away; it’s true, you could argue this is one of the very few benefits of the Boruto anime's progress being so heavily stifled by the manga. Regardless, Boruto spent a long time overcoming the shortcoming of his main-character power-up not showing up until nearly 100 episodes in by relying on his wits and teamwork. test with Kakashi; if you recall, Team 7 took that test and essentially passed by luck because Sasuke and Sakura didn't abandon Naruto, but Boruto grasped the true purpose of that test right away: it was meant to see if they understood teamwork. Now that the manga has reached this point, I finally understand the level of resolve Boruto had when he said, "Even so, I'm still a ninja," in the first episode. Naruto endured the cold glares of his villagers growing up , while Boruto has endured the cold glares of netizens; the scale of this is simply incomparable. Boruto is so disliked, and its protagonist so resented, is that the creators give off the feeling of forcefully extending the story and milking an old IP. Coming up with all this random stuff isn't Boruto's fault; the aliens were something the original series brought in anyway. But speaking of this, people might play their trump card. What is it? I mean, who hasn't felt anxious about their own lack of strength when they were young and wanted to take a shortcut? Plus, I think Boruto must have been afraid that if he didn't perform well enough or got eliminated, he'd be scrutinized and told, "Like father, like son; you're nothing compared to your great father." The important thing is learning and growing from mistakes, but Boruto isn't allowed to have any human flaws, or the typical recklessness that comes with.

that age. And the reason for that is simply because he is the son of Naruto Uzumaki . Wow, doesn't it feel like the fiction and reality just connected? See what I mean? However, the biggest problem with the Boruto manga is that it's a monthly release— only one chapter a month—yet the anime puts out four episodes a month. This meant that the Boruto anime was destined to have a massive amount of filler from the start. Those who have watched Naruto or Bleach know very well how insufferable the filler arcs can be. There are also episodes like the Parent-Child Day that focus on family warmth, which are all great to watch. So, I must emphasize that the. Boruto anime's original content is definitely not trash through and through . It's just a fact that it's padded with a lot of filler. You have to watch about ten episodes just to find one that's truly good. Why can't Boruto get hyped? This, this is the reason. Just think about it: if you were trying to start a fire, but you were forced to take a five-minute break every two seconds, how could the fire ever catch on? like Demon Slayer, Jujutsu Kaisen, or Bleach: TYBW, with tight, well-paced seasons of 12 to 24 episodes. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入解析熱門動畫《電馭叛客：邊緣行者》第二季的評價兩極現象，探討中文圈與英語圈觀眾反應差異的原因。
  • 詳細梳理第二季四大主角（維科、塔利亞、羅曼、D）的角色弧線與劇情定位。
  • 提供客觀的無雷與有雷深度心得，並結合遊戲原作設定（如「摩羯」晶片與相關專有名詞）進行全面點評。

摘要

影片開頭由創作者井川一針對《電馭叛客：邊緣行者》第二季推出後的社群風向進行探討。他注意到中文圈與英語圈的評價出現截然不同的反差，英語圈多數給予正面稱讚，而中文圈則出現較多批評聲浪 [[00:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=6)]。在進入劇透前，影片前半段為無雷心得，探討第二季在故事敘事上的嘗試與特點 [[00:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=30)]。

第二季的核心定位與結構差異

主創巴爾托斯澤爾在訪談中指出，第一季是從「零到有」的成長故事，曲線是上升的；而第二季則是從「有到一無所有」的故事，曲線向下 [[01:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=72)]。第二季捨棄了第一季單一主角的視角，改由四大主角的故事線互相交織，嘗試開創新的敘事路線 [[01:44](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=104)]。然而，故事後期的多線發展未能完全撐起全局，導致部分觀眾認為主線不清、節奏過快 [[01:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=114)]。

核心問題：關鍵道具「摩羯」的設定缺陷

影片指出第二季最大的問題來源在於核心道具「摩羯」（Kaprici，音譯）晶片。它相當於第一季的「沙德威斯坦」，但在設定上有三個致命問題 [[03:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=186)]： 能力過於抽象：使用者插上後會獲得雷電與念動力等過於萬能的超能力，缺乏明確性 [[03:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=200)]。 反客為主：後期主線劇情過度圍繞在摩羯的爭奪上，反而將四大主角的個人曲線晾在一邊 [[04:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=259)]。 過度仰賴遊戲設定：摩羯涉及真人靈魂電子化等遊戲原作設定，對於未玩過遊戲的觀眾而言，容易產生專有名詞過多、難以帶入的問題 [[04:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=277)]。

四大主角深度解析與劇情走向

影片隨後進入劇透環節，詳細剖析四位主要角色的故事與命運 [[06:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=417)]： 維科（King）：以第一季另一種結局設定（神經狂亂但活下來）為起點，從巔峰跌落谷底。雖然無台詞的視覺對照表現出色，但後期戲份被稀釋，淪為推進劇情的配角 [[08:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=509)]。 塔利亞：叛逆的改造少女，與羅曼共同擔當浪漫情感線。最終因摩羯生成為最終 Boss，但劇情轉折略顯混亂 [[10:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=643)]。 羅曼：最接近觀眾視角（POV）的角色，在革命暴動中扮演道德中心，也是情感核心的見證者 [[12:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=730)]。 D（賽博佐助）：實質上的第二季真主角，因族人遭旋戰幫團滅而踏上復仇之路。最終選擇放下仇恨與內疚，戴著虛擬女友展開新的人生 [[13:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=816)]。

總結與評價

總體而言，創作者認為第二季雖然在執行面上存在瑕疵，使情感衝擊力道不如第一季，但其探討「為何而活」而非「為何而死」的對比仍具美感 [[17:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=1038)]。影片呼應主題，反思夜城或許也能擁有不同於第一季的結局 [[17:34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0zcJg4uBFCE&t=1054)]。相關影片資訊可參考：【電馭叛客:邊緣行者2】深度解析！中文圈罵爆, 英語圈吹爆？誰說夜城不能有快樂結局？｜井川一。

摘要

異世界題材作品的流水線困境

作者在評點新番時，首先討論了《轉生為哥布林》等異世界作品。作者指出該作設定充斥既視感，從主角因救人車禍轉生，到繼承親友遺願化為外掛技能，發展幾乎與《關於我轉生變成史萊姆這檔事》雷同，因此決定將其列入棄番名單。此外，針對部分融入金融經濟冷知識或傳統退婚、神明召喚的異世界作品，作者認為其缺乏獨創性與張力，劇情流於公式化龍傲天套路，僅能給予偏低的評分。

在進入大作點評前，作者穿插分享了對《新楓之谷》懷舊內容的感動，回味起搭船前往天空之城、挑戰三轉試煉的往日情懷，隨後正式帶出備受期待的壓軸續作。

《電馭叛客：邊緣行者》第二季的群像魅力

相較於前作圍繞單一主角，作者認為《電馭叛客：邊緣行者 2》開創了全新的獨立篇章。故事聚焦於因神經狂暴化被逐出幫派的 King、全義體少女 Talia、背負滅門仇恨且招式酷似佐助的青年，以及熱愛攝影的 Roman 等四名新世代邊緣行者。作者盛讚本作戲份分配均衡，即使身處機械充斥的賽博龐克世界，故事核心依舊蘊含濃厚的人性溫度，並特別推崇兼具復古與酷帥魅力的全新女主角 Talia，果斷給予 S 級評價。

校園戀愛續作的風格轉變與降級

最後，作者探討了 Netflix 獨佔的校園戀愛作品《冰之壁》第二季。作者分析本作不同於作者前作純粹撒糖的風格，反而更偏向傳統少女漫畫的胃痛戀愛四角關係，充斥校園霸凌、誤會與拖沓的情節推進。儘管角色依然保有高情商的魅力，但劇情節奏在同地打轉過久，反而是直率爭取情感的情敵學妹更具吸引力，也因此作者最終將該作由原先的 S 級下調至 A 級。

  • 快速掌握當季多部話題新番與續作的優缺點分析及評級變化。

  • 剖析異世界題材公式化問題，以及校園戀愛作品在情節編排上的轉折與評價。

摘要

異世界題材作品的流水線困境

作者在評點新番時，首先討論了《轉生為哥布林》等異世界作品。作者指出該作設定充斥既視感，從主角因救人車禍轉生，到繼承親友遺願化為外掛技能，發展幾乎與《關於我轉生變成史萊姆這檔事》雷同，因此決定將其列入棄番名單。此外，針對部分融入金融經濟冷知識或傳統退婚、神明召喚的異世界作品，作者認為其缺乏獨創性與張力，劇情流於公式化龍傲天套路，僅能給予偏低的評分。

在進入大作點評前，作者穿插分享了對《新楓之谷》懷舊內容的感動，回味起搭船前往天空之城、挑戰三轉試煉的往日情懷，隨後正式帶出備受期待的壓軸續作。

《電馭叛客：邊緣行者》第二季的群像魅力

相較於前作圍繞單一主角，作者認為《電馭叛客：邊緣行者 2》開創了全新的獨立篇章。故事聚焦於因神經狂暴化被逐出幫派的 King、全義體少女 Talia、背負滅門仇恨且招式酷似佐助的青年，以及熱愛攝影的 Roman 等四名新世代邊緣行者。作者盛讚本作戲份分配均衡，即使身處機械充斥的賽博龐克世界，故事核心依舊蘊含濃厚的人性溫度，並特別推崇兼具復古與酷帥魅力的全新女主角 Talia，果斷給予 S 級評價。

校園戀愛續作的風格轉變與降級

最後，作者探討了 Netflix 獨佔的校園戀愛作品《冰之壁》第二季。作者分析本作不同於作者前作純粹撒糖的風格，反而更偏向傳統少女漫畫的胃痛戀愛四角關係，充斥校園霸凌、誤會與拖沓的情節推進。儘管角色依然保有高情商的魅力，但劇情節奏在同地打轉過久，反而是直率爭取情感的情敵學妹更具吸引力，也因此作者最終將該作由原先的 S 級下調至 A 級。

  • 快速掌握當季多部話題新番與續作的優缺點分析及評級變化。
  • 深入了解《電馭叛客：邊緣行者》第二季的全新主角陣容與觀影亮點。
  • 剖析異世界題材公式化問題，以及校園戀愛作品在情節編排上的轉折與評價。

摘要

異世界題材作品的流水線困境

作者在評點新番時，首先討論了《轉生為哥布林》等異世界作品。作者指出該作設定充斥既視感，從主角因救人車禍轉生，到繼承親友遺願化為外掛技能，發展幾乎與《關於我轉生變成史萊姆這檔事》雷同，因此決定將其列入棄番名單。此外，針對部分融入金融經濟冷知識或傳統退婚、神明召喚的異世界作品，作者認為其缺乏獨創性與張力，劇情流於公式化龍傲天套路，僅能給予偏低的評分。

在進入大作點評前，作者穿插分享了對《新楓之谷》懷舊內容的感動，回味起搭船前往天空之城、挑戰三轉試煉的往日情懷，隨後正式帶出備受期待的壓軸續作。

《電馭叛客：邊緣行者》第二季的群像魅力

相較於前作圍繞單一主角，作者認為《電馭叛客：邊緣行者 2》開創了全新的獨立篇章。故事聚焦於因神經狂暴化被逐出幫派的 King、全義體少女 Talia、背負滅門仇恨且招式酷似佐助的青年，以及熱愛攝影的 Roman 等四名新世代邊緣行者。作者盛讚本作戲份分配均衡，即使身處機械充斥的賽博龐克世界，故事核心依舊蘊含濃厚的人性溫度，並特別推崇兼具復古與酷帥魅力的全新女主角 Talia，果斷給予 S 級評價。

校園戀愛續作的風格轉變與降級

最後，作者探討了 Netflix 獨佔的校園戀愛作品《冰之壁》第二季。作者分析本作不同於作者前作純粹撒糖的風格，反而更偏向傳統少女漫畫的胃痛戀愛四角關係，充斥校園霸凌、誤會與拖沓的情節推進。儘管角色依然保有高情商的魅力，但劇情節奏在同地打轉過久，反而是直率爭取情感的情敵學妹更具吸引力，也因此作者最終將該作由原先的 S 級下調至 A 級。
